mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) compresses risk-free rates, reducing the discount rate for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is consistent across the current low-rate environment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.25% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the annualized CPI inflation rate (from CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals an impending monetary tightening that causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 2.5% (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a persistently low federal funds rate (<=0.25%) and elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicates a monetary policy stance that is accommodative despite a weak labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary accommodation with weak labor market
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS <= 0.25% and UNRATE > 5.0%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive forward returns as the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain an accommodative monetary policy, preventing a rate hike that would otherwise depress equity valuations. This effect is most pronounced in the current economic cycle.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) is associated with stronger economic growth, which supports equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between INDPRO and 60-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1200.0 thousand units, it signals a strong housing market that typically leads to positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days as the economy shows resilience.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1200.0, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When residential sales (RSAFS) exceed 400,000 million dollars and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1200.0 thousand units, it signals a robust housing market that drives positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS > 400000 and HOUST > 1200.0, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly growth rate in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% (annualized) signals strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 quarterly growth rate > 2.0% (annualized), SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).
